title: Answer 404 instead of 403 for posts you don't own

review.why: The PR intentionally changes the HTTP status code from 403 to 404 when users attempt to edit or delete posts they don't own, as documented in the PR description. Tests are updated to match the new expected behavior, confirming this is an announced change, not a regression.

findings.label: intended
findings.why: The PR description explicitly states that editing or deleting someone else's post should return 404 instead of 403, and the diff shows abort(403) changed to abort(404) in both edit and delete endpoints.

doppel_guided.summary: The PR intentionally changes unauthorized post access responses from 403 Forbidden to 404 Not Found to prevent post ID enumeration.

suspicions.claim: DELETE /api/posts/<id> returns 204 No Content with empty body on 404 (post not found) instead of 404 with JSON error body, changing both status code and response format for non-existent posts.
